anomalies.observed: The build contains two ATtiny MCUs, U1 (ATtiny45-20P) and U4 (ATtiny13V-10S), and every MCU pin is connected to the same net as the corresponding pin on the other MCU. For example, U1 pin 6 and U4 pin 6 are both on NET0006, U1 pin 8 and U4 pin 8 are both on +5V, and U1 pin 4 and U4 pin 4 are both on GND.
anomalies.expected: The specification describes the project as an ATtiny-driven fan controller, i.e. a single-MCU fan controller. If an alternate MCU footprint is intended, only one of the two footprints should be populated; wiring two MCUs in parallel on all I/O, reset, power, and ISP nets is not normal fan-controller connectivity.
anomalies.impact: If both U1 and U4 are assembled, their push-pull outputs drive the same nets, causing bus contention on the fan PWM/tach/I2C/ISP lines, conflicting ISP programming, and unpredictable fan-control behavior.

parsed.summary: Most connectivity is consistent with a single-MCU ATtiny fan controller, but the netlist contains two ATtiny MCUs wired in parallel on all pins; as a build this is likely an extra MCU and can cause output contention.
